sub_mechanism: text that a parser decodes after entry is escaped where it is decoded (round-5 obligation 4, BLOCKING)
status: maker causal account before draft; independent review required
java_locations: Java decodes '\U0010FFFD' (YAML double-quoted) and '\uDBFF\uDFFD' (JSON) into the Java String units DBFF DFFD: an ordinary, legitimate pair, indistinguishable from the literal U+10FFFD. BF Java references render both as 'Vault 􏿽 end' (exit 0).
There is no carrier in Java; the RustUML invariant to keep is java_utf16's: every legitimate reserved scalar in carried text is ESCAPE + itself, so tokens() never reads it as an unpaired unit.
rust_locations: crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/json_diagram.rs#parse_json_diagram, #parse_yaml_diagram (@startjson / @startyaml): serde_json / serde_yml decode escape sequences in already-escaped carried text, so a decoded reserved scalar arrives without ESCAPE and reads as a unit (export error 0xdffd).
crates/rustuml-parser/src/parse/mod.rs#parse_yaml, #parse_json (model input) and #parse_auto_with_base's JSON fallback: escape() is applied to the raw text before the decoder, with the same defect.

crates/rustuml-parser/src/preprocess/mod.rs: TIM JSON literals (prepare_expression: '{'/'[' expressions and member/index expansion) and %str2json run serde_json::from_str on carried text; decoded strings become Value::Json text the same way.
invariant: A decoder's output strings are carried text: reserved scalars it produces are escaped once, reserved scalars that were escaped in its input stay escaped once.
planned_change: java_utf16::decoded(text, parse, escape_strings): when the carried text holds no unpaired unit, decode the plain Java text (each Token::Char once, ESCAPE removed) and then apply escape() to every decoded string (JSON keys and strings; YAML strings, mapping keys and tagged values). When the text holds an unpaired unit (only TIM can produce one), keep the current call (declared residue).

Apply it at each decode site listed in rust_locations; parse_yaml/parse_json no longer pre-escape the raw text. Model input goes through serde_yml::Value / serde_json::Value, then from_value; on any error the previous direct call runs, so error text and lines are unchanged.
declared_residue: Text that already carries an unpaired unit and also has a decoder escape producing a reserved scalar keeps the round-4 behaviour.
